name: git
description: Run sandboxed git commands on the project. Input: {"args": ["status", "--porcelain"]}. Allowed: status, diff, log, show, add, commit, ls-files, rev-parse, branch, worktree. push, reset, rebase, checkout, clean, rm, fetch, merge, revert, stash are denied by default; setting agent.git_remote_ops lifts push, merge and checkout for git. Runs at the run's root, the same directory the file tools resolve paths against, so plain `add`/`commit` stage exactly the files you edited. Git global options that take a value (-C <path>, --git-dir <path>, --work-tree <path>) are honored for inspecting another worktree. Do not try to isolate your own work by adding a worktree and pointing git at it: only git would move, the file tools would not, so your edits would keep landing in the run's root while `git -C <wt> status` reported that worktree as clean. Isolation is the harness's (clanker run --worktree), and when it is on, the run's root already IS the worktree. Returns {"ok": bool, "code": int, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "..."}.
llm_description: Run sandboxed git commands. {"args":["status","--porcelain"]}. Allowed: status, diff, log, show, add, commit, ls-files, rev-parse, branch, worktree.
